From 80721776c5af6f6dce7d84ba8df063957aa425a2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nuno Sa <nuno.sa@analog.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Apr 2024 17:42:13 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] iio: adc: axi-adc: make sure AXI clock is enabled

We can only access the IP core registers if the bus clock is enabled. As
such we need to get and enable it and not rely on anyone else to do it.

Note this clock is a very fundamental one that is typically enabled
pretty early during boot. Independently of that, we should really rely on
it to be enabled.

Fixes: ef04070692a2 ("iio: adc: adi-axi-adc: add support for AXI ADC IP core")
Signed-off-by: Nuno Sa <nuno.sa@analog.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240426-ad9467-new-features-v2-4-6361fc3ba1cc@analog.com
Cc: <Stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Jonathan Cameron <Jonathan.Cameron@huawei.com>

diff --git a/drivers/iio/adc/adi-axi-adc.c b/drivers/iio/adc/adi-axi-adc.c
index 9444b0c5a93c..f54830658da8 100644
--- a/drivers/iio/adc/adi-axi-adc.c
+++ b/drivers/iio/adc/adi-axi-adc.c
@@ -161,6 +161,7 @@ static int adi_axi_adc_probe(struct platform_device *pdev)
 	struct adi_axi_adc_state *st;
 	void __iomem *base;
 	unsigned int ver;
+	struct clk *clk;
 	int ret;
 
 	st = devm_kzalloc(&pdev->dev, sizeof(*st), GFP_KERNEL);
@@ -181,6 +182,10 @@ static int adi_axi_adc_probe(struct platform_device *pdev)
 	if (!expected_ver)
 		return -ENODEV;
 
+	clk = devm_clk_get_enabled(&pdev->dev, NULL);
+	if (IS_ERR(clk))
+		return PTR_ERR(clk);
+
 	/*
 	 * Force disable the core. Up to the frontend to enable us. And we can
 	 * still read/write registers...
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/iio/adc/adi-axi-adc.c`**
   - Added a new variable `struct clk *clk;` to hold the clock reference.
   - Introduced a call to `devm_clk_get_enabled(&pdev->dev, NULL);` to retrieve and enable the AXI clock. This ensures that the clock is enabled before accessing the IP core registers.
   - Added error handling for the clock retrieval, returning an error if the clock cannot be obtained.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `adi-axi-adc.c` are directly related to ensuring that the AXI clock is enabled before any operations are performed on the IP core registers. This change addresses a fundamental requirement for the proper functioning of the ADC driver, as it prevents potential access issues that could arise if the clock is not enabled. The patch emphasizes the importance of managing the clock within the driver itself rather than relying on external components or earlier boot processes to handle it. This change is a fix for a previously introduced feature (as noted in the `Fixes` tag), indicating that the initial implementation did not adequately ensure the clock was enabled, leading to potential bugs.

Although the code does include a call to `devm_clk_get_enabled(&pdev->dev, NULL);`, it is placed after the initialization of the register map and before the read/write operations. This means that if the clock is not enabled prior to accessing the registers, it can lead to undefined behavior or errors, which is the root cause of the bug described.         Root cause:
        The bug arises from the failure to ensure that the AXI clock is enabled before accessing the IP core registers. Without the clock being enabled, any attempts to read or write to the registers can lead to undefined behavior or errors, as the necessary clock signal for operation is not present. This oversight can result in the driver not functioning correctly, as it relies on the clock being active to perform its tasks.
